observations: A large rounded form fills most of the teal ground, built from overlapping red, yellow, black, and blue shapes; a white-outlined square sits upper-left with red cross-hatching inside it.
Near the center, concentric red-outlined rectangles spiral inward toward a dense knot of white and black lines, flanked by broad areas of dark teal and yellow.
White looping lines scatter across the right half, open against the tighter layered marks elsewhere; a row of white rectangles runs along the lower center.
reading: The teal ground holds a compressed mass of competing marks: red rectangles tighten toward a white core while yellow and black shapes push outward to the edges. The white square at upper left reads as a cooler, more contained zone against the heat of the central red. The row of white rectangles at the bottom anchors the structure with a blunt horizontal note, offering a pause the rest of the image refuses.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, the teal ground links this work to nnxyz nifty faces #120, which shares the same background color and a wide tooth row. Title neighbor nnxyz nnotb #173 uses a bright blue ground instead, shifting the feeling despite comparable density of layered marks.

connections.reason: Both works share a teal ground and a prominent horizontal band of white rectangular tooth-like shapes along the lower edge, a pairing the collector links to scrimshaw's incised white-on-dark quality.

Title neighbor nnxyz nnotb #173 uses a comparable rounded-form structure and layered multicolor marks, but its bright blue ground and pink passages produce a lighter feeling against #174's darker teal and heavier red.

lookingQuestion: Where does your eye move when it reaches the loose white loops on the right — does it return to the tight spiral at center, or drift toward the white square at upper left?
ambiguities: The white-outlined square at upper left contains marks that could read as a face or as pure geometric layering; no external evidence resolves this.
nnxyz nnotb #175 was inspected but its distinct blue ground, floral dot border, and open circular composition offered no strong formal parallel to #174 beyond shared artist and collection.
